free_tier.stated: a network connection plus the ability to host services on it; no storage quota because there is no storage product

egress.terms: donated transit from upstream peers; the wiki is explicit that NYC Mesh cannot detect or prevent traffic monitoring by those upstreams

interface_detail: a routed internet connection; you run your own server behind it
tooling: standard Linux/nginx/S3 behind your own router
chaining: member-hosted services are a stated goal - 'we allow for fast uploads as well as downloads, so members of our community can host content and services rather than only consume them'
limits_note: Cost is $240 equipment + $50 install leader ($290), or $110 + $50 subsidised ($160), plus a monthly donation. Realistically it is an ISP substitute for one household, not a storage provider: it gives you symmetric upload and a routable presence, so it improves the *serving* half of the problem for one location, and adds nothing to the 20 TiB problem. Also geographically bounded to NYC.
reliability_note: Depends on donated upstream transit and volunteer installers; no SLA and no redundancy.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
